\section{Canonical equations}
\label{sec:equations}

\subsection{Peak-normalized analytic family}
\label{sec:analytic-family}

Let $J_1$ be the first-order Bessel function of the first kind, and define its
first positive zero exactly by
\begin{equation}
  j_{1,1}=\min\{x>0:J_1(x)=0\}.
  \label{eq:first-bessel-root}
\end{equation}
The rounded decimal $3.831706$ is only a nonnormative approximation to
$j_{1,1}$.  Define the collision-free peak-normalized function
\begin{equation}
  \mathcal{J}(x)=
  \begin{cases}
    2J_1(x)/x, & x\ne0,\\
    1, & x=0.
  \end{cases}
  \label{eq:peak-jinc}
\end{equation}
For $r'_a=r/s_a$, the generic SCI-JINC coefficient is
\begin{equation}
  \kappa_a(r'_a; a_a,b_a,c_a,(r_{\max})_a)
  =\mathcal{J}\!\left(\frac{2\pi r'_a}{a_a}\right)
   \exp\!\left[-\left(\frac{2r'_a}{b_a}\right)^{c_a}\right]
   \mathcal{J}\!\left(\frac{j_{1,1}r'_a}{(r_{\max})_a}\right).
  \label{eq:analytic-kernel}
\end{equation}
Equation~\eqref{eq:analytic-kernel} has $\kappa_a(0)=1$.
$a_a$ scales the first JINC argument, $b_a$ scales the generalized-exponential
envelope, $c_a$ is its exponent, and $(r_{\max})_a$ places the first zero of
the second JINC factor.  Analytic zeros and finite signed lobes are retained.
The square-cache rule, rather than a radial cutoff, determines membership.

\subsection{Exact discrete point-phase and WCS operator}
\label{sec:discrete-operator}

Let the exact AST continuous FITS pixel coordinate in the target JINC WCS be
$\boldsymbol{u}_i=(x_i,y_i)$.  Integer FITS coordinates denote pixel centers.
The exact rounded cache center is
\begin{equation}
  \boldsymbol{c}_i=
  \left(\left\lfloor x_i+\tfrac12\right\rfloor,
        \left\lfloor y_i+\tfrac12\right\rfloor\right).
  \label{eq:rounded-center}
\end{equation}
Thus an exact half-pixel tie rounds toward the positive coordinate axis.  The
scientific owner retains this directional convention as part of the selected
discrete operator.  The
residual phase is
\begin{equation}
  \boldsymbol{\phi}_i=\boldsymbol{u}_i-\boldsymbol{c}_i
  \in[-\tfrac12,\tfrac12)^2.
  \label{eq:residual-phase}
\end{equation}
For $n_{\mathrm{sub}}\ge1$, each axis uses the exact half-open bins
\begin{align}
  B_q & =\left[-\tfrac12+\frac{q}{n_{\mathrm{sub}}},
                    -\tfrac12+\frac{q+1}{n_{\mathrm{sub}}}\right),
        \qquad q\in\{0,\ldots,n_{\mathrm{sub}}-1\},
        \label{eq:phase-bin}\\
  q(\phi) & =\left\lfloor
          n_{\mathrm{sub}}(\phi+\tfrac12)\right\rfloor,
        \label{eq:phase-index}\\
  \widehat{\phi}_q &=-\tfrac12+
          \frac{q+\tfrac12}{n_{\mathrm{sub}}}.
        \label{eq:phase-representative}
\end{align}
The two axis indices form $\boldsymbol{q}_i$, and their midpoint
representatives form $\widehat{\boldsymbol{\phi}}_i$.  Every positive integer
$n_{\mathrm{sub}}$ is permitted under
\texttt{SCI-JINC-DEC-PHASE-CENTER-001}.  The half-open upper-bin convention is observable:
when $n_{\mathrm{sub}}$ is even, an exact $\phi=0$ selects
$q=n_{\mathrm{sub}}/2$ and
$\widehat\phi=+1/(2n_{\mathrm{sub}})$, with the sign interpreted in the exact
target-WCS axis orientation.  No special case substitutes a zero
representative.
The exact logical cache mapping is
\begin{equation}
  \beta_i=q_{i1}+n_{\mathrm{sub}}q_{i2},\qquad
  \mathcal{K}_{i\boldsymbol d}=(\beta_i,d_1,d_2),
  \label{eq:phase-cache-index}
\end{equation}
equivalently $(q_{i1},q_{i2},d_1,d_2)$ with axis 1 varying fastest. Physical
storage may use any proven value-preserving bijection of this logical key.

Base v0.1 requires an affine tangent-plane target WCS with exact pixel matrix
$\mathbf{M}$ satisfying
\begin{equation}
  \mathbf{M}^{\mathsf T}\mathbf{M}=\Delta^2\mathbf{I},
  \qquad \Delta>0.
  \label{eq:square-wcs-metric}
\end{equation}
The exact $\mathbf{M}$ retains axis order, signs, rotation, and handedness;
Equation~\eqref{eq:square-wcs-metric} prohibits representing an anisotropic or
skewed metric by a scalar pixel size.  With finite destination domain
$\mathcal{D}=\{1,\ldots,N_x\}\mathbin{\times}\{1,\ldots,N_y\}$, define
\begin{align}
  h_a &=\left\lceil\frac{s_a(r_{\max})_a}{\Delta}\right\rceil,
       \label{eq:cache-half-width}\\
  \boldsymbol{d}&\in\{-h_a,\ldots,h_a\}^2,
       \qquad \boldsymbol{p}=\boldsymbol{c}_i+\boldsymbol{d}.
       \label{eq:square-offsets}
\end{align}
For every retained square offset, the exact discrete point-phase radius is
\begin{equation}
  \widehat r_{i\boldsymbol{d}}
   =\left\|\mathbf{M}
      (\boldsymbol{d}-\widehat{\boldsymbol{\phi}}_i)\right\|_2,
  \qquad
  \widehat r'_{i\boldsymbol{d}}=
      \widehat r_{i\boldsymbol{d}}/s_a,
  \label{eq:discrete-radius}
\end{equation}
and $\kappa_{ip}$ is Equation~\eqref{eq:analytic-kernel} evaluated at
$\widehat r'_{i\boldsymbol{d}}$.  The occurrence passes the center-domain gate
only when $\boldsymbol{c}_i\in\mathcal{D}$; a square pixel is retained only
when $\boldsymbol{p}\in\mathcal{D}$.  These integer-domain predicates, rather
than footprint overlap or a radial cutoff, determine geometry membership.

For an occurrence at an exact integer pixel center, both residual-phase
components are zero.  When $n_{\mathrm{sub}}$ is even, the upper-bin rule in
\texttt{SCI-JINC-DEC-PHASE-CENTER-001} and
Equation~\eqref{eq:square-wcs-metric} therefore give, at
the nominal central offset $\boldsymbol d=\boldsymbol0$,
\begin{align*}
  \widehat r_{i\boldsymbol0}
    &=\frac{\Delta}{\sqrt{2}\,n_{\mathrm{sub}}},\\
  \kappa_{i,\boldsymbol c_i}
    &=\kappa_a\!\left(
       \frac{\Delta}{\sqrt{2}\,n_{\mathrm{sub}}s_a};
       a_a,b_a,c_a,(r_{\max})_a\right).
\end{align*}
The nominal central cache element is thus evaluated at this exact nonzero
radius and shall not be replaced by the zero-radius limit
$\kappa_a(0)=1$.  For odd $n_{\mathrm{sub}}$, exact zero phase has midpoint
representative zero and the nominal central offset evaluates the analytic
limit at zero.

\subsection{Signed estimator}
\label{sec:signed-estimator}

For the exact occurrence population of one bundle,
\begin{align}
  w_{ip} &= \omega_i\kappa_{ip},
    \label{eq:effective-coefficient}\\
  N_p &= \sum_i I_{ip}\omega_i\kappa_{ip}z_i,
    \label{eq:numerator}\\
  C_p &= \sum_i I_{ip}\omega_i\kappa_{ip},
    \label{eq:normalization}\\
  Q_p &= \sum_i I_{ip}\omega_i\kappa_{ip}^{2},
    \label{eq:quadratic}\\
  m_p &= \frac{N_p}{C_p},
    \label{eq:map-estimate}\\
  A_{pi} &= \frac{I_{ip}\omega_i\kappa_{ip}}{C_p}.
    \label{eq:operator}
\end{align}
All coupled accumulator terms for one contribution use the same $I_{ip}$ and
the same realized $\kappa_{ip}$ identity.  The normalization is signed.  A
finite negative $C_p$ is admissible; exact $C_p=0$ is not a zero-sky result.

\subsection{Conditioning and local support}
\label{sec:conditioning}

Define construction-state quantities
\begin{align}
  D_p &= \sum_i I_{ip}\left|\omega_i\kappa_{ip}\right|,
    \label{eq:absolute-sum}\\
  \rho_p &= \frac{|C_p|}{D_p}, \qquad D_p>0.
    \label{eq:cancellation-ratio}
\end{align}
For exact arithmetic, $0\le\rho_p\le1$.  Accepted local support requires
the algebraic predicate
\begin{equation}
  \operatorname{AlgSupport}_p=
  \bigl[\text{required inputs and }N_p,C_p,Q_p\text{ are finite}\bigr]
  \land[Q_p>0]\land[C_p\ne0].
  \label{eq:algebraic-support}
\end{equation}
A finite-precision numerical realization additionally requires
\begin{equation}
  \operatorname{NumAdeq}_p=
  \bigl[\mathcal{E}_p\text{ is a valid certificate under }
        \mathcal{P}_{\mathrm{NA}}\bigr]
  \land
  \bigl[\mathcal{E}_p\models\mathcal{P}_{\mathrm{NA}}\bigr].
  \label{eq:numerical-adequacy}
\end{equation}
The exact profile supplies the observable, norm, domain, error propagation,
near-zero rule, simultaneous or worst-case interpretation, and pass/fail
inequality.  No such owner-approved profile or matching certificate is
admitted or supplied by this source packet, so
Equation~\eqref{eq:numerical-adequacy} is presently typed unavailable.  In
particular, no approximate fidelity scale promotes a near-cancellation pixel.
$D_p$ remains construction state rather than a numerical map-plane role; any
future certificate is referenced by the compact generative record $G_a$.
A passing $\mathcal{P}_{\mathrm{NA}}$/$\mathcal{E}_p$ pair establishes only
finite-precision fidelity to the exact selected discrete SCI-JINC oracle over
the profile's declared domain.  It does not establish scientific adequacy of
$s_a$, $a_a$, $b_a$, $c_a$, $(r_{\max})_a$, $n_{\mathrm{sub}}$, or square
truncation; source-response or beam fidelity; photometric or astrometric
performance; optimality; observational validation; response/covariance
fidelity; readiness; or production authority.  Qualification of a TolTEC
parameter set is a separate scientific and observational program.

\subsection{Coefficient-squared temporal accounting}
\label{sec:coefficient-time}

The sole authorized base-v0.1 coefficient-squared temporal-accounting product
is \path{jinc_coefficient_squared_time}, defined by
\begin{equation}
  T_p^{(\kappa^2)}
  =\sum_i I_{ip}\frac{\kappa_{ip}^{2}}{f_{s,i}}.
  \label{eq:kappa-time}
\end{equation}
It is nonnegative and has unit seconds.  The squared object is $\kappa_{ip}$,
not $\omega_i$ or $w_{ip}$.

\subsection{Conditional mathematics retained for future science}
\label{sec:conditional-math}

The following identities do not create base-v0.1 products.  For an exact
available realized PTC-grid source-template response, the fixed-state response
is
\begin{equation}
  \mathbf{R}_{\mathrm{JINC,fixed}}
  =\mathbf{A}_{\mathrm{JINC}}
   \mathbf{H}_{\mathrm{PTC,fixed}}.
  \label{eq:fixed-state-response}
\end{equation}
The exact signal membership is used and the already realized PTC companion
receives the JINC operator exactly once.  A PTC full-procedure finite
difference with JINC held fixed, a JINC re-resolved procedure response, and a
whole-chain response are distinct families and must not be substituted for
Equation~\eqref{eq:fixed-state-response} or for one another.

If and only if an
exact PTC family establishes $\omega_i=\operatorname{Var}(z_i)^{-1}$ for
mutually independent admitted occurrences,
\begin{align}
  \operatorname{Var}_{\mathrm{formal}}(m_p) &= \frac{Q_p}{C_p^2},
    \label{eq:conditional-variance}\\
  W_{\mathrm{formal},p} &= \frac{C_p^2}{Q_p},
    \label{eq:conditional-weight}\\
  \operatorname{Cov}(m_p,m_{p'})
   &=\frac{\sum_i I_{ip}I_{ip'}\omega_i\kappa_{ip}\kappa_{ip'}}
           {C_pC_{p'}}.
    \label{eq:conditional-covariance}
\end{align}
For a general available upstream covariance,
\begin{equation}
  \mathbf{C}_{\mathrm{JINC}}
  =\mathbf{A}_{\mathrm{JINC}}
   \mathbf{C}_{\mathrm{PTC}}
   \mathbf{A}_{\mathrm{JINC}}^{\mathsf T}.
  \label{eq:general-covariance}
\end{equation}
Inverse-square units alone do not establish inverse variance, independence,
precision, covariance authority, or significance.  A covariance state, if a
future use authorizes one, is exactly one of complete numerical, partial,
symbolic, summarized, lineage-resolvable, or unavailable and declares every
omitted term.  Missing covariance is never zero or independence.  Response,
variance, formal-weight, and covariance companions remain deferred until a
concrete scientific use separately authorizes them.
